unit_objectives: listen to a personal testimony on the benefits of a hobby and recreational activities
talk about hobbies and recreational activities and their benefits
revise consonant sounds and practise tongue twisters
skim a text for the main ideas and answer questions
use vocabulary pertaining to recreational activities
use phrasal verbs and prepositional phrases
write a formal letter requesting recreational facilities for a community
develop sociability, collaboration, cooperation and openness

source_sections.title: Hobbies, listening and consonant sounds
source_sections.source_scope: Unit opening, Listening and speaking, Speech work
verified_content: The unit asks learners to discuss popular recreational activities and their benefits.
A listening activity is built around a fictional personal testimony linked to fashion design.
Voiced consonants are described as involving vocal-cord vibration; unvoiced consonants are described as not involving it.
The source explicitly lists examples of voiced and unvoiced consonants.

source_sections.title: Skimming and identifying main ideas
source_sections.source_scope: Reading notes and first two personal stories
verified_content: The skimming note recommends reading the title/subheadings, looking at pictures/charts and reading the first sentence of each paragraph.
Elenwa describes music and caring for a dog as hobbies that help with stress and relationships.
Lily describes dressmaking as a childhood hobby that later helps balance her life as a paediatrician.

source_sections.title: Reading stories about the benefits of hobbies
source_sections.source_scope: Elenwa, Lily, Teleu and Eyole plus comprehension
verified_content: Teleu describes gardening, floral arrangements, environmental beauty, improved skills and additional family income.
Eyole describes drama as helping overcome shyness and improve self-confidence, participation and peer respect.
The source provides true/false comprehension statements for all four stories.

source_sections.title: Vocabulary, phrasal verbs and prepositional phrases
verified_content: Vocabulary includes stress, hobby, balance, outfit, shy, self-confidence and nurture.
The phrasal-verb exercise includes calm down, come across, eat out, hang around, shut up, turn down, shape up, call off, break into and figure out.
The prepositional-phrase exercise contrasts forms such as at the end of, in the world, in a loud voice, on time, at a party and in my opinion.

source_sections.title: Writing a formal letter about recreational facilities
verified_content: The task asks for a formal letter to the mayor about the lack of recreational facilities.
The learner should address well-being, mental and physical health, relationships, income, community contribution and personal help.
The requested length is about 200 words in 4-5 paragraphs and the letter should close politely.

limitations.issue: The listening questions are present, but the full teacher-read testimony is not available in the supplied extraction; only a short contextual note about Kibonen Nfi is visible.
limitations.runtime_action: Do not invent answers to the listening-comprehension questions.

limitations.issue: Speech-work rules and tongue twisters are present as text, but no validated audio accompanies the extraction.
limitations.runtime_action: Conceptual voiced/unvoiced knowledge may be auto-scored; pronunciation quality is self-evaluated only.

limitations.issue: The extracted formal-letter annotations contain internally inconsistent guidance about 'Yours faithfully'/'Yours sincerely'.
limitations.runtime_action: Do not auto-score that sign-off rule; teach only source-supported structure and the instruction to close politely.
